disclaimer.strong: This page compares pregnancy and cycle apps.
disclaimer.rest: It is educational, not medical advice, and no clinician has reviewed it yet.

doctor: Call your hospital or doctor if you have heavy bleeding, severe pain, trouble breathing, a severe headache, blurred vision, a high fever, or reduced baby movement after movements have started.
title: Babymigo Alternatives in Nigeria: Four Apps Compared
description: Compare four Babymigo alternatives for pregnancy in Nigeria. See week by week guidance, clinic tools, communities, prices and local support.
share: If you want another option beside Babymigo, compare four pregnancy apps by clinic tools, week by week guidance, community and price.
kicker: For Nigerian women choosing support for a first pregnancy
answer: Choose Wholesome Girlies for Nigerian clinic questions, checklists and a pregnancy plan paid once. Choose What to Expect or BabyCentre for daily updates and large parent communities. Choose Pregnancy+ for a kick counter, contraction timer and a birth plan. Keep Babymigo if you want its Nigerian provider directory or forum.

image.alt: Illustration of Zainab comparing pregnancy apps

picks.name: Wholesome Girlies
picks.label: Best for a Nigerian first pregnancy
picks.suits: You want week by week guidance, questions for antenatal visits and checklists that fit Nigeria.
picks.price: The tools need no payment. The First Pregnancy Plan is ₦5,700 (about $4) early-bird or ₦13,700 (about $10) standard, paid once.
can: See your pregnancy week from your due date.
Print questions for each antenatal visit.
Build your birth plan and hospital bag list.
cannot: There is no doctor consultation or provider directory.

picks.name: What to Expect
picks.label: Best for daily articles and community
picks.suits: You want daily pregnancy updates and a large parent community.
picks.price: The Nigerian App Store lists the app with no payment and shows no in-app purchase price.
can: See week by week development videos.
You can keep your symptoms, weight, baby movements and medicines in one log.
cannot: Its care guidance is not written for Nigerian clinic schedules.

picks.name: BabyCentre
picks.label: Best for daily updates through baby's first year
picks.suits: You want daily pregnancy updates and baby guidance in the same app.
picks.price: The Nigerian App Store lists the app with no payment and shows no in-app purchase price.
can: Use a kick tracker and contraction timer.
Join birth clubs and community groups.
cannot: Its guidance is not written for Nigerian clinic schedules.

picks.name: Pregnancy+
picks.label: Best for pregnancy tools
picks.suits: You want a kick counter, contraction timer, hospital bag list and birth plan in one app.
picks.price: Purchases on the Nigerian App Store run from ₦4,900 (about $4) to ₦24,900 (about $19).
can: Use a kick counter and contraction timer.
Make a birth plan and hospital bag list.
See week by week three dimensional baby models.
cannot: Its guidance is written for a global audience.

why: Babymigo is strong when you want a Nigerian provider directory, a large forum or a live antenatal class. Another app may suit you when you want daily tracking, a kick counter, a birth plan or a plan you can keep.
criteria: Check whether the app follows Nigerian antenatal care.
Check whether you need an account before using the tools.
Check whether you need a forum, a live doctor or a self-paced plan.

faq.q: What is the best Babymigo alternative in Nigeria?
faq.a: Choose by the job. Wholesome Girlies suits clinic preparation. What to Expect and BabyCentre suit daily reading and community. Pregnancy+ suits pregnancy tools.
Yes. Babymigo has a Nigerian provider directory and forum that the other options on this page do not replace.
